answer: Bonded escrows bind each identity’s stake to accountable keys. When k identities coordinate equivocation, correlated evidence triggers a penalty proportional to k², not k, so splitting control among aliases raises aggregate loss. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to forfeiture and asymmetric depreciation to remaining capital, making a sybil swarm costlier than honest participation. No operator can wander into a haven by relabeling identities; the claim that aliases dilute risk is a fable.
